svg.title: Five randomised trials in older glioblastoma patients: length of course against median survival
svg.desc: Schematic scatter plot placing five randomised trials in older glioblastoma patients on one pair of axes: length of the course in weeks on the horizontal axis, median survival in months on the vertical axis. Keime-Guibert 2007 (aged 70 and over, KPS 70 or more, n=81): supportive care alone 16.9 weeks (about 3.9 months) versus supportive care plus 50 Gy in 28 fractions 29.1 weeks (about 6.7 months), hazard ratio 0.47 (0.29 to 0.76), P = 0.002; the paper reports weeks, converted to months here. Roa 2004 (aged 60 and over, n=100): 60 Gy in 30 fractions 5.1 months versus 40 Gy in 15 fractions 5.6 months, P = .57, no difference shown. Nordic 2012 (aged 60 and over, three randomised arms): 60 Gy in 30 fractions 6.0 months, 34 Gy in 10 fractions 7.5 months, temozolomide alone without radiotherapy 8.3 months; temozolomide versus standard radiotherapy hazard ratio 0.70 (0.52 to 0.93), p = 0.01. Roa 2015 (elderly or frail, n=98, median follow-up only 6.3 months): 40 Gy in 15 fractions 6.4 months versus 25 Gy in 5 fractions 7.9 months, P = .988, no difference shown. Perry 2017 (aged 65 and over, n=562, both arms 40 Gy in 15 fractions, drawn with the heaviest markers): radiotherapy alone 7.6 months versus radiotherapy plus temozolomide 9.3 months, hazard ratio 0.67 (0.56 to 0.80), P < 0.001. Two annotations are required on the figure. First, the MGMT strata of Perry: methylated (n=165) 13.5 versus 7.7 months, hazard ratio 0.53 (0.38 to 0.73), P < 0.001; unmethylated (n=189) 10.0 versus 7.9 months, hazard ratio 0.75 (0.56 to 1.01), P = 0.055, which did not reach statistical significance. Second, the steroids in Roa 2004: 49 per cent of the 60 Gy in 30 fractions arm needed an increase in steroid dose versus 23 per cent of the 40 Gy in 15 fractions arm (chi-squared P = .02), while survival showed no difference (P = .57). The caption line reads: the course gets shorter and the survival does not fall, and that is what it can be shortened means. The closing warning: what decides this is performance status, not the year on the birth certificate; the non-inferiority of the short course applies to glioblastoma patients aged 60 and over and cannot be turned into old means shorten it; and people with poor performance status, largely bedbound, have been excluded from almost every randomised trial, so that in that group no randomised trial has ever compared best supportive care with active radiotherapy or chemotherapy.

g.text: FIVE RANDOMISED TRIALS IN OLDER PATIENTS
What most people are offered today is a
short course of radiotherapy plus the
drug
The horizontal axis is the length of the course in weeks; the vertical
axis is median survival in months. The course gets shorter and the
survival does not fall — that is what "it can be shortened" means.
The five trials differ in entry criteria, era and endpoints, so the points
must not be joined up across trials.

aged 65 and over, n=562; both arms had 40 Gy in 15 fractions｜hazard ratio 0.67 (0.56 to
The one that had to come first: Keime-Guibert randomised patients to no radiotherapy as
well, and the answer was that radiotherapy helps. Only with that established does the
question of shortening arise.
The MGMT strata in Perry 2017 (the second layer, and it matters)
Methylated (n=165): 13.5 versus 7.7 months, hazard ratio 0.53 (0.38 to 0.73), P < 0.001.
Unmethylated (n=189): 10.0 versus 7.9 months, hazard ratio 0.75 (0.56 to 1.01), P =
0.055 — which did not reach statistical significance. Adding the drug is not the same
size of effect in the two strata.
The steroids in Roa 2004 (the difference is not only in survival)
Patients needing an increase in steroid dose: 49% in the 60 Gy in 30 fractions arm, 23%
in the 40 Gy in 15 fractions arm (chi-squared P = .02). Survival showed no difference
(P = .57) — the difference showed up here instead.
What decides this is performance status, not the year on the birth
certificate
The non-inferiority of the short course applies to glioblastoma patients aged
60 and over; it cannot be turned into "old means shorten it". And people with
poor performance status, largely bedbound, have been excluded from almost
every randomised trial; in that group no randomised trial has ever compared
best supportive care with active radiotherapy or chemotherapy — the
conversation there is a different one.
Schematic, redrawn from Keime-Guibert 2007, Roa 2004, Malmström 2012
(Nordic), Roa 2015 and Perry 2017; the cohorts, designs and endpoints of the
underlying studies differ, so the data points must not be compared directly.
